scope: PR #177 (15 files): task-receipt.mjs (write/check/export per-task receipts, store at ~/.claude/esk/receipts); receipt-grounding.mjs (extracted grounding primitives) + check-skill-receipt.mjs refactored to import them; docs/specs/skill-application-receipt.md section 11; ADR-0097; 7 BDD scenarios + task-receipt.steps.mjs + the shared end-its-turn dispatcher refactor in checker-fail-closed.steps.mjs; datastore + coverage log; test/task-receipt.test.mjs; package.json; CHANGELOG. The reviewer verified fail-closed on every check refusal, the hash-tie, full coverage, behavior-preserving refactor, and a discriminating suite; it raised four findings (2 medium, 2 low) plus minor notes, all fixed before this entry.

boundary.evidence: one CLI (write/check/export) owns per-task receipts, next to the PR receipt it mirrors; resolution + fail-closed translation centralized.

ownership.evidence: the per-session store is the single owner of per-task application facts (one file per session); completeness vs the selection is disclosed when no selection is given, never silently passed (F2 fix).

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins only; the grep's only hits are the domain term session_id and prose 'per pull request', no web concern.

error-handling.evidence: every check refusal exits 2 (empty, stale/copied hash, uncovered file, ungrounded quote, skill_file_sha256 mismatch, applied-file-outside-change, missing selected skill, expired waiver, malformed). F1 fix: a skill/session name of '.' or '..' is rejected before the join and the resolved skill file is realpath-contained (traversal closed, matching the PR gate). F5 fix: the changed-file hash read is wrapped so a read error refuses (exit 2), keeping the 0/2 contract.

boundary.evidence: the grounding primitives (slug, section, whitespace, >=8-word threshold, single-heading quoteUnderHeading) are extracted to one module.

ownership.evidence: F3 fix: the shared owner is the primitives (the drift-prone parts); each gate composes them for its own shape (per-task: one heading+quote; PR: several sections+quotes). The module, spec, and ADR say 'shared primitives', not 'one place', so the claim matches the code.

dependency.evidence: pure text functions; no fs/process in receipt-grounding.

error-handling.evidence: the check-skill-receipt refactor is behavior-preserving: node --test test/skill-receipt.test.mjs is 27 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; the only code delta is md.split -> String(md).split (a safe hardening).

boundary.evidence: integration tests spawning the real CLI over sandboxed skills dirs and work folders.

error-handling.evidence: discriminating: against a no-op check (always exit 0) every refusal test flips, and the positive test asserts the 'accepted' output a no-op never prints. Extended for the fixes: '..' name refused, completeness-disclosed output, directory-as-changed-file refused, '..' session refused, waiver export carries approver+expires. 19 pass.

boundary.evidence: 7 @audience:agent scenarios drive the real task-receipt.mjs; the shared 'the agent tries to end its turn' step is a dispatcher (world.endTurn) so it serves both #183 and #177 without ambiguity.

ownership.evidence: step defs write only temp fixtures; no step-text collision across the two step files.

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins; spawns the real CLI.

error-handling.evidence: every scenario that uses the dispatcher has a Given/And that sets world.endTurn; the dispatcher throws if unset (fail loud). 25/25 scenarios pass on the harness.

boundary.evidence: spec section 11 documents the per-task schema, store, checker, export; ADR-0097 records the decision + honest limits; package.json wires test/task-receipt.test.mjs (guarded by all-tests-wired).

ownership.evidence: one ADR; the CHANGELOG entry is additive under 1.3.1.

error-handling.evidence: the spec and ADR name the limits: reports a refusal but the finish hook (#174) turns it into a stopped turn and must itself fail closed; changed-list/selection are caller-supplied (same trust as the PR gate's diff); without a selection completeness is disclosed as not-checked.

findings.finding: the bare /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/ admits '..' (and '.'), so a crafted skill or session name could escape the skills dir / store via path.join - a grounding bypass with a planted or parent-level SKILL.md, contradicting the guard's own promise and the spec threat model.
findings.resolution: fixed: isSafeName rejects '.' and '..' before the join (for both skill names and session ids), and the applied branch realpath-checks that the resolved skill file stays inside the skills dir, matching the sibling PR gate. Tests added for a '..' skill name and a '..' session.

findings.finding: completeness was enforced only when --selection was passed, silently downgrading the PR gate's every-skill-covered guarantee; an agent could submit a one-skill receipt and pass clean with no selection.
findings.resolution: fixed: without --selection the gate now DISCLOSES 'completeness NOT checked' in its OK line (the way the PR gate discloses diff-binding without a diff), never a silent pass; the finish hook (#174) will pass the router's required-skill list (#175). Test added asserting the disclosure.

findings.finding: the 'one place' claim overclaimed: check-skill-receipt imports only the primitives and re-implements the composed quote decision inline (it concatenates several sections and checks several quotes), so the composed decision lived in two places.
findings.resolution: fixed (honest claim): the shared owner is the primitives (slug, section, whitespace, threshold) - the drift-prone parts - and each gate composes them for its own shape. The module comment, spec section 11, and ADR-0097 now say 'shared primitives', matching the code.

findings.finding: export mapped waived -> not-applicable carrying only the waiver reason, dropping approver and expires, so the audit trail (who approved the skip, when it lapses) was lost at the status level.
findings.resolution: fixed: the exported why now carries reason, approver, and expires for a waived skill. Test added.

minorNotes: changed-list and selection are caller-supplied (no git diff outside a repo): the hash-tie defends against copying, not an honest-but-incomplete list - documented in the spec and ADR as the same trust property as the PR gate's diff, not a bug.

export fills a missing why/what with a self-labeled placeholder that satisfies the PR gate's nonEmpty check; grounding (quotes/anchors/where) is real and human review is mandated, so impact is low (left as is).
recordedByPath lookup is case-sensitive; on Windows a case-only path difference fails CLOSED (no false accept), a robustness nit left as is.
